questions.q: What fundamentally makes Salesforce a CRM rather than just a database?
options: It organizes data specifically around managing relationships and interactions with customers and prospects
It can only store contact names and phone numbers
It requires no internet connection to use
It is exclusively for tracking employee payroll
questions.explain: CRM stands for Customer Relationship Management — Salesforce structures its data model (Leads, Accounts, Contacts, Opportunities, Cases) around the customer lifecycle, not generic data storage.

questions.q: What's the core difference between Sales Cloud and Service Cloud?
options: Service Cloud can only be used by companies with fewer than 10 employees
Sales Cloud manages the sales pipeline (leads, opportunities); Service Cloud manages post-sale customer support (cases)
There is no real difference — they are the same product with different names
Sales Cloud is free and Service Cloud requires a paid license for every user
questions.explain: Sales Cloud is built around the revenue-generating objects like Leads and Opportunities, while Service Cloud is built around Cases and support processes — many orgs run both on the same platform.

questions.q: What is the AppExchange?
options: A tool for exchanging currency values between Salesforce orgs
A deprecated feature that Salesforce removed in 2020
Salesforce's marketplace for pre-built apps, integrations, and components that extend an org
The billing page where admins pay their monthly Salesforce invoice
questions.explain: The AppExchange is Salesforce's app marketplace — third-party and Salesforce-built packages (free and paid) that add features like data quality tools, dashboards, and industry-specific functionality.

questions.q: Why does it matter to a data analyst that Salesforce is a multi-tenant platform with configurable editions?
options: Because it means SOQL queries run differently depending on the edition
Because multi-tenancy means every company shares the exact same data with each other
Because editions only affect the color scheme of the interface
Because the exact fields, objects, and features available differ by edition and by org configuration, so no two orgs' data models are guaranteed to look identical
questions.explain: Editions (Essentials, Professional, Enterprise, Unlimited) unlock different features and limits, and each org is separately customized — an analyst can't assume a field or object exists just because it did in a different org.

questions.q: A Lead in Salesforce represents what?
options: An unqualified prospect who hasn't yet been vetted as a real sales opportunity
A closed-won deal
A support ticket submitted by an existing customer
A custom object with no standard fields
questions.explain: Leads sit at the top of the sales funnel — raw, unqualified prospect information — before qualification converts them into an Account, Contact, and (usually) an Opportunity.

questions.q: When a Lead is converted in Salesforce, what typically happens?
options: The Lead record is permanently deleted with no trace
The Lead's data is used to create an Account and Contact, and optionally an Opportunity, while the original Lead record is marked converted
The Lead becomes a Case automatically
Nothing changes — conversion is purely cosmetic and creates no new records
questions.explain: Lead conversion is a one-way process that maps Lead fields onto a new (or existing) Account and Contact and can create an Opportunity, preserving the original Lead as a read-only converted record for reporting.

questions.q: What does the Opportunity object primarily track?
options: A list of all Contacts at a company regardless of sales activity
The technical configuration of a user's profile
A potential deal in progress, including its stage, amount, and expected close date
A scheduled meeting on a rep's calendar
questions.explain: Opportunities represent deals moving through a sales pipeline, tracked by Stage (e.g., Prospecting, Negotiation, Closed Won) — this is the object most pipeline and forecast reports are built on.

questions.q: What is a Campaign used for in Salesforce, and how does it typically relate to Leads and Contacts?
options: It is a type of custom field that stores a single dollar amount
It automatically merges duplicate Contact records
It replaces the need for an Account object entirely
It tracks a marketing initiative and links to Leads/Contacts through Campaign Members, enabling ROI and influence analysis
questions.explain: Campaigns represent marketing efforts (an email blast, a trade show); the CampaignMember junction connects Leads and Contacts to Campaigns so analysts can measure response rates and pipeline influenced by that effort.

questions.q: What does a Case represent in Salesforce's Service Cloud data model?
options: A customer's support issue, question, or complaint being tracked to resolution
A signed contract between two Accounts
A marketing email template
A type of report chart
questions.explain: Cases are the core Service Cloud object — each one tracks a single support interaction from creation through statuses like New, In Progress, and Closed.

questions.q: Why does understanding the Case lifecycle (statuses, escalation paths, SLAs) matter for reporting on Service Cloud data?
options: Because Case status has no effect on any reports
Because metrics like resolution time and SLA compliance are calculated from timestamps tied to specific status transitions, so an analyst must know what each status actually means operationally
Because all Cases automatically close themselves after 24 hours
Because Case data can only be viewed by the agent who created the record
questions.explain: Metrics like average handle time or SLA breaches depend on correctly interpreting when a Case entered and left each status — misreading the lifecycle produces misleading service analytics.

questions.q: What's the key structural difference between a standard object and a custom object in Salesforce?
options: Custom objects cannot have any relationships to other objects
Standard objects can only be viewed by system administrators
Custom objects are created by an org's admins and their API names end in __c, while standard objects (like Account or Contact) ship built into the platform
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
questions.explain: Salesforce appends __c to the API names of custom objects and custom fields to distinguish org-specific additions from the standard schema every org starts with.

questions.q: Which of these is a Salesforce field type that stores a single option chosen from a predefined list?
options: Long Text Area
Auto Number
Geolocation
Picklist
questions.explain: A Picklist field constrains entry to a defined set of values, which is why picklist fields are so often used for grouping and filtering in reports.

questions.q: What do Record Types control in Salesforce?
options: Which picklist values and page layout a user sees for records of a given business process on the same object
The physical database table a record is stored in
Whether a field is required at the database level
The currency exchange rate applied to a record
questions.explain: Record Types let a single object (e.g., Opportunity) present different picklist value sets and page layouts for different business processes, like 'New Business' versus 'Renewal' deals.

questions.q: In the Salesforce data model, what is the difference between a Lookup relationship and a Master-Detail relationship?
options: Lookup relationships allow up to 10 related records while Master-Detail allows unlimited
Master-Detail ties a child record's security and lifecycle to its parent (deleting the parent deletes children), while Lookup relationships are looser and independent
Master-Detail can only be used on custom objects, never standard ones
There is no functional difference between them
questions.explain: Master-Detail enforces that the child record inherits sharing from the parent and is deleted if the parent is deleted, whereas a Lookup is a more independent, optional reference between two records.

questions.q: What is a junction object used for in Salesforce?
options: Storing a single admin's login credentials
Replacing the need for any standard objects
Modeling a many-to-many relationship between two objects using two Master-Detail relationships
Encrypting sensitive fields automatically
questions.explain: Because native relationships are one-to-many, a junction object (like CampaignMember, which links Campaigns and Leads/Contacts) sits in the middle with two Master-Detail relationships to represent many-to-many connections.

questions.q: What does Schema Builder let an analyst or admin do?
options: Write and execute SOQL queries against production data
Directly edit records in bulk
Configure Stripe billing for the org
Visually see and explore how objects relate to each other across the org
questions.explain: Schema Builder is a visual, drag-and-drop diagram of an org's objects and their relationships — a fast way for an analyst to understand an unfamiliar org's data model before writing any queries.

questions.q: What is the role hierarchy primarily used for in Salesforce?
options: Controlling record visibility — users higher in the hierarchy can see records owned by users below them
Determining which fonts appear in the user interface
Setting a user's monthly login limit
Assigning currency conversion rates
questions.explain: The role hierarchy is a vertical structure for record access: unless sharing rules restrict it, a manager's role can see everything owned by roles below them, mirroring how many sales and service organizations are structured.

questions.q: What's the difference between a Profile and a Permission Set in Salesforce?
options: Profiles are only for admins; Permission Sets are only for regular users
Every user has exactly one Profile controlling baseline access, while Permission Sets grant additional permissions on top and can be assigned to many users flexibly
Permission Sets replace the need for a Profile entirely in every org
Profiles control record ownership while Permission Sets control field colors
questions.explain: A user must have one and only one Profile, which sets baseline object/field access, while Permission Sets are additive and reusable across users regardless of their Profile — a more flexible way to grant extra access.

questions.q: What do sharing rules do that the role hierarchy and org-wide defaults alone cannot?
options: Delete records that haven't been accessed in 90 days
Change a field's data type
Extend record access to specific additional users or groups based on criteria or ownership, beyond the default hierarchy
Automatically convert Leads into Opportunities
questions.explain: Sharing rules widen access beyond what org-wide defaults and the role hierarchy already grant — for example, sharing all Opportunities owned by the West team with the East team for visibility, without changing ownership.

questions.q: What does field-level security (FLS) control that object-level and record-level security do not?
options: Which records a user can see in a list view
Whether a user can log in from a mobile device
The default sort order of a report
Whether a specific user can view or edit a particular field, even if they can access the record itself
questions.explain: A user might have access to an Account record but still be blocked from seeing a specific field, like an internal credit-risk score — that's field-level security, layered on top of object and record access.
